prompt: Solve for $x$: $5(x - 1) - 2x = 2x + 7$. Give just the number.
hint: Tidy the left side completely before moving anything across the equals sign.

hints.text: Tidy the left side completely before moving anything across the equals sign.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up by distributing only: $5(x - 1)$ is $5x - 5$. Now the left side is $5x - 5 - 2x = 3x - 5$. Much friendlier!
Distribute and combine: $5x - 5 - 2x = 3x - 5$, so the equation is $3x - 5 = 2x + 7$. Subtract $2x$, then add $5$.
$x - 5 = 7$, and adding $5$ to both sides gives the solution $x = 12$.

explanation: Distribute the $5$ to both terms in the parentheses: $5(x - 1) = 5x - 5$.
Combine the like terms on the left side: $5x - 5 - 2x = 3x - 5$.
Subtract $2x$ from both sides to get $x - 5 = 7$, then add $5$ to get $x = 12$.
Check: the left side is $5(11) - 24 = 31$ and the right side is $2(12) + 7 = 31$, so $x = 12$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Tidy each room first
steps: Treat each side like a messy room: you cannot compare them until both are tidy.
Left room tidied: $3x - 5$. Right room is already tidy: $2x + 7$.
Now the equation $3x - 5 = 2x + 7$ is a simple both-sides problem: $x = 12$.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ Dodge the trap
steps: Rushing to move terms across before tidying loses the −5: mixing 5x − 1 − 2x is where this one goes wrong.
Clean your own side first: 5(x − 1) − 2x = 3x − 5. Only THEN cross the river: 3x − 5 = 2x + 7 gives x = 12.
